DNA methylation sequencing, whole-body TIPIN knockout mouse hydrodynamic injection models, RNA-seq, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, protein stability and ubiquitination assays, and patient‑derived xenograft and patient‑derived organoid models were used. TIPIN was upregulated by DNA hypomethylation in liver cancer and associated with poor prognosis. TIPIN promoted liver cancer initiation and progression in vivo. Mechanistically, TIPIN binds Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and competes with E3 ligase c‑Cbl for the Tyr1045-containing interface, thereby repressing c‑Cbl-mediated EGFR ubiquitination and degradation and activating downstream ERK1/2 signaling to facilitate tumor proliferation and metastasis. TIPIN depletion accelerates EGFR turnover and sensitizes liver cancer cells to lenvatinib. TIPIN stabilizes EGFR via competitive binding to the Tyr1045 interface, restricting its ubiquitin-dependent degradation to drive liver cancer progression and lenvatinib resistance. Targeting the TIPIN-EGFR axis could be an effective therapy for liver cancer.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid-derived small extracellular vesicles reveal a compartment-specific diagnostic signature for NSCLC leptomeningeal metastasis.
abstract: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a devastating complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet timely diagnosis remains challenging because conventional approaches, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology, have limited sensitivity, particularly at initial presentation. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), as nanoscale carriers of protected regulatory cargo, have emerged as promising substrates for liquid biopsy. However, in anatomically compartmentalized central nervous system malignancies, the extent to which disease-associated sEV-miRNA signals are preserved across biofluids remains unclear. We profiled sEV-associated miRNAs by small RNA sequencing in CSF and plasma samples from NSCLC patients with clinically adjudicated LM status (NC, LM-, and LM+), including paired specimens where available. Biofluid-specific miRNA programs were characterized using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and diagnostic models were developed using machine learning with Random Forest and LASSO-based feature selection. Model performance was evaluated in an independent validation cohort relative to final adjudicated LM status and compared with initial and cumulative MRI and CSF cytology assessments. CSF-derived sEV-associated miRNAs showed markedly stronger disease-stratification capacity than plasma-derived signals (ARI = 0.813 vs. 0.255; cluster purity = 0.868 vs. 0.694), revealing profound biofluid asymmetry. Network analysis identified a dominant LM-associated module in CSF (r = 0.74, P = 9 × 10⁻⁷) with limited preservation in plasma, indicating that LM-related vesicle-associated molecular programs are compartment-restricted. From this CSF-specific nanoscale vesicle signature, we derived a four-miRNA diagnostic panel comprising hsa-let-7e-5p, hsa-miR-30d-5p, hsa-miR-486-5p, and hsa-miR-375. In the independent validation cohort, the single-sample sEV-miRNA panel achieved an AUC of 0.935, with 86.4% sensitivity and 87.5% specificity. By comparison, initial MRI and initial CSF cytology showed sensitivities of 50.0% and 77.3%, respectively, whereas cumulative MRI and cumulative CSF cytology showed sensitivities of 70.0% and 86.4%, respectively. CSF-derived sEV-associated miRNAs encode an LM-proximal molecular program that is not faithfully captured in plasma, underscoring the importance of biofluid compartmentalization in nanobiotechnology-based biomarker discovery. Our findings establish a compartment-aware sEV-miRNA diagnostic strategy for accurate LM detection and provide a conceptual framework for extracellular vesicle-based molecular diagnostics in central nervous system malignancies.

title: Alterations and interactions: effects of Porphyromonas gingivalis and Bifidobacterium bifidum on c-MYC/CCAT2 gene expression in colorectal cancer.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common and life-threatening malignancies worldwide. Despite extensive research, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying CRC progression remain incompletely understood. Accumulating evidence indicates that complex interactions among oncogenic signaling pathways, non-coding RNAs, and the gut microbiota play a pivotal role in CRC pathogenesis. Among oral microbiota, Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) has been implicated in tumorigenesis through the induction of chronic inflammation and activation of oncogenic pathways. This study aimed to investigate the expression levels of the lncRNA CCAT2 and the c-MYC, as well as to evaluate the relative abundance of P. gingivalis and Bifidobacterium bifidum (B. bifidum) in colorectal cancer tissues compared with adjacent normal tissues. DNA and RNA were extracted from biopsy specimens obtained from 40 patients with CRC and 25 healthy controls. Complementary DNA (cDNA) was synthesized using commercial kits, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was conducted to measure the expression levels of CCAT2 and c-MYC, as well as the relative abundance of the 16S rRNA genes of P. gingivalis and B. bifidum. Expression levels of lncRNA CCAT2 and c-MYC were significantly higher in CRC tissues than in normal samples (p < 0.05). Likewise, the relative abundance of P. gingivalis was significantly increased, whereas B. bifidum abundance was significantly decreased in CRC tissues (p < 0.05). In the combined study population (CRC and healthy controls), Spearman's rank correlation analysis demonstrated significant positive correlations between P. gingivalis abundance and both CCAT2 and c-MYC expression, as well as a significant inverse correlation between B. bifidum abundance and CCAT2 expression. However, in the CRC subgroup, only the positive correlation between P. gingivalis abundance and c-MYC expression remained statistically significant. These findings demonstrate significant associations between P. gingivalis colonization, B. bifidum depletion, and oncogenic molecular alterations in CRC. Although associations involving CCAT2 were evident in the combined cohort, only the relationship between P. gingivalis abundance and c-MYC expression persisted within the CRC subgroup, suggesting that some observed correlations may primarily reflect differences between CRC patients and healthy controls. Owing to the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn. Further mechanistic and longitudinal studies are warranted to validate these findings and to explore the clinical utility of microbiota-based biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

title: An integrated bioinformatics analysis reveals that targeted activation of IL7R may reduce influenza A virus infection risk in patients with depression.
abstract: Depression has been associated with increased susceptibility to influenza; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed to assess the causal relationship between depression and influenza. Differential expression genes (DEGs) analyses were performed using Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets related to influenza A virus (IAV) infection and depression. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis were employed to explore underlying mechanisms and identify hub genes involved in depression combined with IAV infection. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve validation and external datasets were conducted to validate the key gene. Immune infiltration and correlation analyses, together with single-cell RNA (scRNA) sequencing and virtual knockout (KO) simulation, were used to investigate altered immune cells and their associations with the key gene. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to screen potential compounds targeting the key gene. Finally, in vitro experiments using IAV-infected Jurkat T cells further validated the roles of the key gene and candidate compound. MR analysis indicated that depression exerts a detrimental causal effect on influenza susceptibility. 24 overlapping DEGs and 13 hub genes were identified through DEG analysis. PPI, GO and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed these genes were mainly enriched in immune and inflammatory pathways. IL7R was identified as a key gene and was positively correlated with multiple T-cell subsets while negatively correlated with macrophages, as determined by ROC curve analysis, external validation datasets, and immune infiltration analysis. scRNA-seq analysis demonstrated that IAV infection reduced CD4 + and CD8 + T cells infiltration while increasing macrophage-like monocytes abundance and significantly downregulating IL7R expression, particularly in CD4 + T cells. Virtual KO of IL7R led to the upregulation of MT-CYB and MT-CO1 in CD4 + T cells. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that sanguinarine exhibited the strongest binding affinity for IL7R and maintained stable interaction. In vitro experiments further confirmed that sanguinarine reversed IAV-induced downregulation of IL7R and reduced viral replication. IL7R may serve as a potential therapeutic target, and sanguinarine represents a promising candidate for the treatment of depression combined with IAV infection through immune modulation.

title: Serum estradiol, reproductive timing, and melanoma prevalence among women: population-based evidence and single-cell transcriptomic insights.
abstract: Evidence linking female reproductive factors and circulating estradiol with melanoma has been inconsistent. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of US women in NHANES 2009-2023. Exposure-specific analytic samples were constructed for age at menarche, pregnancy history, natural menopause age, and serum estradiol. Associations with prevalent melanoma were examined using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression. XGBoost with Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used as a complementary prediction analysis. Two melanoma single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets (GSE269936 and GSE115978) were analyzed to examine the patient-level association between inferred ESR2 activity and E2F/G2M proliferation-related transcriptional activity. Low estradiol levels (0-20 pg/mL) were associated with higher odds of prevalent melanoma [adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 3.382; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.304-8.773; P = 0.013], and late menarche (>14 years) was also associated with higher odds (adjusted OR = 2.074; 95% CI = 1.118-3.846; P = 0.021). Pregnancy history was not significantly associated with melanoma prevalence. The association for premature menopause could not be estimated because no melanoma cases occurred in this category. Low estradiol was the highest-ranked encoded feature by global SHAP importance (mean |SHAP| = 0.157). Across 10 patients inferred ESR2 activity was inversely correlated with the composite proliferation score (pooled r = -0.250; 95% CI = -0.392 to -0.095; P = 0.006). Lower estradiol levels and later menarche were associated with higher odds of prevalent melanoma. The single-cell finding requires prospective and functional studies are needed to determine the biological and clinical relevance of these findings.

title: Genetic variants in WDR4 influencing m7G modification are associated with prostate cancer susceptibility.
abstract: The associations between genetic variants in N7-methylguanosine (m7G)-related genes and prostate cancer susceptibility remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between WDR4 genetic variants and prostate cancer risk and explored their potential regulatory relevance. A discovery cohort from the PLCO study and an independent validation cohort from the PRACTICAL consortium were analyzed using logistic regression models. Functional annotation, expression quantitative trait locus analysis, RNA secondary-structure prediction, gene-expression analysis, survival analysis, and single-cell transcriptomic analysis were performed to investigate the potential biological relevance of associated variants. The rs8130270 variant in WDR4 was associated with prostate cancer susceptibility in the discovery cohort (OR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.82-0.96, P(FDR) = 2.65 × 10-2) and was validated in the PRACTICAL cohort (OR = 0.98, 95% CI = 0.97-1.00, P = 4.16 × 10-2). The rs8130270 C allele was associated with lower WDR4 expression in prostate tissue. WDR4 expression was higher in prostate cancer tissues, and high WDR4 expression was associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 1.67, 95% CI = 1.06-2.64, P = 2.00 × 10-2). Single-cell analysis showed that WDR4 was expressed across multiple immune and tumor-associated cell populations. These findings suggest that rs8130270 in WDR4 may contribute to prostate cancer susceptibility through effects on WDR4 expression and provide genetic evidence supporting a potential role of WDR4-related m7G regulation in prostate cancer.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte state remodeling in paraquat-associated Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is an environmentally relevant herbicide associated with neurotoxicity and Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, yet the key molecular determinants linking PQ exposure to PD and the cellular states in which these alterations occur remain incompletely understood. We integrated network toxicology, human PD transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, spatial metabolomics, virtual perturbation, model-inferred protein analysis, molecular docking, and tissue validation to characterize PQ-associated molecular and cellular remodeling. Integrating PQ-associated targets with PD-related genes identified 293 candidates, among which prostaglandin D2 synthase (PTGDS) was consistently prioritized by random forest, XGBoost, and LASSO, with its PD-associated expression pattern reproduced across the discovery and independent validation cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized Ptgds expression predominantly to oligodendrocytes and identified two PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte (MOL) states with PQ-associated compositional patterns. CytoTRACE placed these PTGDS-enriched populations among relatively mature oligodendrocyte states. Functional analyses revealed distinct state-specific programs, with Ptgds+Mag+ MOL associated with myelin-associated programs, axon ensheathment-related programs, cholesterol metabolism, and lipid transport, whereas Ptgds+Il33+ MOL was linked to neuron-interaction-related programs, synaptic organization, cell adhesion, and neuron-glia communication. Ligand-receptor inference and spatial analyses supported state-specific changes in neuron-glia communication and spatial relationships. Spatial metabolomics showed significantly increased phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin signals in regions with higher inferred representation of Ptgds+Mag+ MOL states. Virtual Ptgds perturbation and scTranslator-based protein prediction further suggested state-specific myelin-lipid and neuron-interaction programs, while molecular docking provided preliminary structural predictions regarding a potential PQ-PTGDS interaction. Immunofluorescence further confirmed PTGDS localization in mature oligodendrocytes within the substantia nigra. Collectively, these findings identify PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte states as cellular contexts associated with PQ-related brain remodeling and extend our understanding of PQ neurotoxicity beyond classical neuron-centered mechanisms. This integrative framework provides mechanistic insight into how an environmental neurotoxicant may reshape myelin-lipid homeostasis and neuron-glia interactions in the context of PD-related brain pathology.

title: Serum anti-POTEE antibodies as a novel serological biomarker for early detection and prognostic stratification in gastrointestinal cancers.
abstract: Given the highly aggressive nature of gastrointestinal cancers, the identification of novel biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis is of considerable clinical importance. Candidate cancer-testis (CT) antigens were first screened using RNA-sequencing data from normal human tissues; candidates showing high commonality across tumor RNA-sequencing datasets publicly available in The Cancer Genome Atlas were subsequently prioritized, and POTEE was identified as a promising target. Recombinant POTEE protein was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified by affinity chromatography, and used as the antigen for serological analysis. Serum levels of anti-POTEE antibodies (s-POTEE-Abs) were significantly elevated in 121 patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 62 patients with gastric adenocarcinoma, and 158 patients with colorectal adenocarcinoma compared with those in 96 healthy donors. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis showed that the diagnostic performance of s-POTEE-Ab was comparable to that of s-p53-Ab, with area under the curve values of 0.832 versus 0.829 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 0.680 versus 0.698 in gastric adenocarcinoma, and 0.735 versus 0.706 in colorectal adenocarcinoma, respectively. In survival analyses, s-POTEE-Ab positivity was associated with poorer overall survival in ESCC and CRAC, but not in GAC. After multivariable adjustment, an independent prognostic association was retained only in CRAC. These findings suggest that s-POTEE-Ab may represent a promising exploratory serological biomarker for gastrointestinal cancers. Its prognostic relevance appears to be cancer-type dependent and requires further validation in independent cohorts.

title: Global burden of chewing-tobacco-attributable oral cancer and genomic-transcriptomic profiling of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors.
abstract: Smokeless chewing tobacco and combustible cigarette smoking are the two primary tobacco-related drivers of lip and oral cavity cancer worldwide, yet global epidemiological registries and public cancer-genomic repositories capture these modalities asymmetrically. We designed a complementary two-component framework to jointly benchmark the macro-epidemiological burden of chewing tobacco and the micro-genomic landscape of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors without conflating their distinct exposures. We analyzed the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 dataset to quantify the global and regional burden of lip and oral cavity cancer attributable to chewing tobacco from 1990 to 2021 and projected age-specific burden to 2050. Separately, in a strictly audited cohort of 299 primary oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) with complete clinical covariates and recorded cigarette smoking history (295 with RNA-seq, 292 with whole-exome sequencing, and 288 with both), we performed multivariable differential expression, mutational signature, co-expression network, immune deconvolution, and nested machine-learning analyses. In 2021, chewing tobacco accounted for 37,507 deaths (95% UI 25,312 to 52,128) and 1,131,637 DALYs (95% UI 773,196 to 1,576,992) globally, with 91.7% of deaths concentrated in South Asia and global annual deaths projected to reach 62,840 by 2050 under age-specific demographic decomposition. In the TCGA cigarette-smoking oral cavity cohort, smoking-exposed tumors exhibited higher tumor mutational burden (TMB, p = 1.3 × 10^-7), enrichment of LRP1B and PIK3CA mutations after TMB adjustment (q = 0.027), activation of cytochrome P450 xenobiotic metabolism, and lower expression of an antiviral/interferon-related co-expression module (MEpurple, r = -0.19, p = 9 × 10^-6), whereas TPM-based quanTIseq immune cell fractions did not pass false-discovery-rate correction (FDR > = 0.05). In leak-free nested holdout evaluation (n = 87), a five-feature Random Forest model achieved an AUC of 0.614 (95% CI 0.492 to 0.728) compared with 0.619 for TMB alone. Chewing tobacco imposes a severe, geographically concentrated oral cancer burden centered in South Asia, while cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors in TCGA display elevated mutational load and altered metabolic-antiviral transcriptional programs without incremental multi-omic classification gain over TMB alone. Because these two components reflect distinct tobacco exposures, the molecular findings in cigarette-smoking tumors do not explain the chewing-tobacco epidemiological burden; rather, they establish a rigorous methodological and molecular reference baseline for future profiling of smokeless-tobacco-associated oral cancer cohorts.

title: Molecular subtyping of brain metastasis-related genes in lung adenocarcinoma via scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq integration: A focus on TPX2.
abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a common complication of advanced lung cancer with extremely poor prognosis. This study aimed to establish a molecular classification system for stratifying non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)-BrM patients and predicting survival, and to identify key BrM-related molecules and elucidate their mechanisms as potential therapeutic targets. We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to construct molecular subtyping models for predicting lung cancer prognosis and immune microenvironment, and to screen key molecules driving BrM. Based on H1299 and PC9-BrM cells, in vitro experiments demonstrated the regulatory role and mechanism of targeting protein for Xklp2 (TPX2) in lung cancer BrM. We identified 20 BrM-associated genes. Consensus clustering based on these genes stratified patients into two subtypes, with patients in Subtype 2 showing significantly worse overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS). Mechanistic analyses revealed marked activation of proliferation-related pathways in Subtype 2. TPX2 was identified as a critical mediator, with significantly elevated expression in BrM lesions compared with primary lung cancer lesions, and TPX2 overexpression correlated with poorer prognosis. Functional assays in H1299 and PC9-BrM cells demonstrated that TPX2 knockdown markedly impaired proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, and invasion. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses and Western blotting validation further indicated that TPX2 likely promotes NSCLC-BrM by activating c-MYC and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process. Our study established a molecular classification system that effectively stratifies NSCLC-BrM patients and predicts survival. Moreover, TPX2 promotes NSCLC-BrM through c-MYC/EMT regulation, offering new insights for targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses suggest a myeloid-associated candidate role of THBS1 in sepsis.
abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of mortality worldwide, and biomarkers that integrate inflammatory dysregulation, immune-cell localization, and prognostic relevance remain limited. To identify a candidate molecule linked to myeloid immune responses in sepsis, we performed an integrated analysis of public bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing data, a small exploratory clinical RNA-sequencing cohort, and compound screening analyses. Differential expression analysis and meta-analysis across public datasets identified THBS1 as a consistently altered transcript in sepsis. In a small exploratory peripheral-blood transcriptomic cohort comprising 23 patients with sepsis and 10 healthy controls, THBS1 was selected for downstream analysis on the basis of its position in the public-data protein-protein interaction network and the subsequent THBS1-focused analyses. The reused clinical RNA-sequencing cohort was retained only as an exploratory description and was not used to claim independent validation. Single-cell analysis suggested that THBS1 expression was more prominent in subsets of myeloid-related cell populations. Survival analysis in an external dataset indicated that high THBS1 expression was associated with poorer outcomes, but this finding should be interpreted as exploratory because formal adjustment for disease severity was not possible. Candidate compounds associated with THBS1 were further prioritized by database mining and molecular docking. This study provides transcriptomic and computational evidence suggesting that THBS1 may be associated with myeloid-related immune activity and adverse prognosis in sepsis. Because the clinical cohort was small, protein-level validation and functional experiments were not performed, and substantial heterogeneity was observed across public datasets, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.
